column1: # Bug-discovery record: one row per probe batch, the input of the reliability exit's discovery-rate
# signal (ROADMAP Phase 1 exit 2m) and of the bug dashboard (scripts/gen/bug_dashboard.py, which
# check_docs_drift.sh runs with --check). Every bug record from 079 on (docs/bugs/NNN_*.md) is
# attributed to exactly one row; whoever files a bug adds it to the batch that found it, or adds that
# batch, in the same commit, and regenerates the dashboard.
# A row is a batch: a bounded piece of probing with a recorded effort, whether or not it found bugs.
# A batch that finds nothing is recorded too: zero rows are the signal.
# Columns (tab-separated, every cell non-empty, "-" for none):
#   date     YYYY-MM-DD, the day the batch ran (the first day for a multi-day batch)
#   kind     one of: hunt, examples, workload, design-proofs, semantics, spec, fuzz, interp-coverage
#            (independent probes: they count toward the discovery-rate signal), or
#            ci, review, follow-on, controls, development (attribution only: they find bugs as a side
#            effect of other work and do not count as probe rounds)
#   probe    what was probed, in a few words
#   effort   the size of the batch as "<N> hours|programs|probes|examples|cases" (a fuzz campaign
#            in hours), or "unrecorded" for history seeded from the bug records; a counting batch
#            from 2026-10-22 on must record it. A quiet counting batch below 4 hours or 10
#            programs is a token batch: recorded, shown, and not counted toward the signal
#   bugs     comma-separated three-digit bug numbers the batch found, or "-"
#   silent   the subset of bugs that are silent (memory-safety violation in accepted code, silent
#            wrong code or wrong value, false proof or claim, authority violation, a gate passing
#            vacuously), or "-"; the rest are loud (rejected valid programs, invalid IR, link
#            failures, interpreter refusals, leaks the checker should reject)
